input: nums is a nonempty Array with length <=10000 and integer values in [0,10000]. k is an integer in [0,10000]. return: The minimum possible maximum-minus-minimum range after choosing exactly one of +k or -k for EACH element. This is not arbitrary adjustment within [-k,k]. A singleton returns 0; the adjusted array is not returned.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a fresh sorted copy is reordered. No actual +/-k updates are made to caller values.
numeric: Adjusted candidate values lie in [-10000,20000], candidate spans in [0,30000], and all indices are exact small integers. The numeric comparator is relational, not subtraction-based.
complexity: O(n+1) work after sorting, considering every boundary between the sorted prefix assigned +k and suffix assigned -k, plus the all-same-sign original range. JavaScript sorting adds T_sort(n) time and O(n+S_sort(n)) auxiliary copied-array/workspace costs; ECMAScript does not prescribe a universal sort complexity. No exponential assignment enumeration is used.
